newsitem.title: COMOROS: Crowd cheers as island governor on Comoros quits.
newsitem.headline: Crowd cheers as island governor on Comoros quits.

text.p: Secessionists on the Indian Ocean island of Anjouan cheered when their governor announced he was resigning on Sunday, witnesses said on Monday.
Colonel Cheikh Allaoui was appointed governor last month by Mohammed Taki, president of the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros, during pro-secession demonstrations on Anjouan.

"I offer you my sincerest apologies and I submit to you my resignation," Allaoui told a rally in his home town of Domoni, 30 km (20 miles) southeast of Anjouan's capital Mutsamudu, according to the witnesses speaking to Reuters by telephone.
Allaoui had supported Anjouan independence but defected to the government in July after a meeting with Taki.
The crowd responded on Sunday with thunderous applause, yelling the slogan "Mkutruwa" (Rupture).
Under the Comoran constitution the governor is the highest political authority on the island.
On Moheli island, which like Anjouan declared independence from the Comoros federation in August, pro-secessionists have given the governor, Hachim Mohammed, until Monday to submit his resignation.
The secessionist-appointed prime minister of Moheli, Soidri Ahmed, said that if he refused to resign he would be forced out.

Islanders on Anjouan and Moheli say they want to return to French rule or become independent because they have received little from the government but poverty and numerous coups since independence from France in 1975.
The poverty in the Comoros, with a population of some 670,000, contrasts with comparative prosperity on the island of Mayotte, which voted against independence in 1975 and remains under French rule.
But France has denounced the secessionist unrest, saying it could destabilise the whole region of Indian Ocean islands.
